summary: The main article describes a copper-catalyzed hydrosilylation of terminal allenes to produce (E)-allylsilanes. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope figures for disubstituted and monosubstituted allenes, and a computational study to explain the observed regio- and stereoselectivity.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Hydrosilylation of terminal allenes. a Challenges in the control of regio- and stereo-selectivity. b Previous work on the transition-metal-catalyzed hydrosilylation of terminal allenes mainly afforded vinyl silanes, branched allylsilanes and ( Z )-allylsilanes as the products. c This work: we report a coppercatalyzed selective hydrosilylation of terminal allenes to access exclusively ( E )-allylsilanes.
items.description: This figure outlines the challenges of allene hydrosilylation, summarizes previous catalytic approaches, and introduces the current copper-catalyzed method for (E)-allylsilanes.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Evaluation of reaction conditions.
items.description: This table details the optimization of catalysts, ligands, and stoichiometry for the hydrosilylation of buta-2,3-dien-2-ylbenzene.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Scope of 1,1-disubstituted allenes.
items.description: This figure displays the substrate scope for various 1,1-disubstituted allenes and diarylsilanes, showing yields and E/Z ratios.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Scope of monosubstituted allenes.
items.description: This figure illustrates the reaction scope for monosubstituted allenes with different silanes, highlighting the high E-selectivity achieved.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Gram scale reaction and downstream transformations.
items.description: This figure demonstrates the scalability of the reaction and various chemical transformations of the (E)-allylsilane products.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Mechanism study.
items.description: This figure presents experimental mechanism studies including deuterium labeling, KIE experiments, and isomerization tests.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Computational study.
items.description: This figure shows DFT calculations and IGM analysis explaining the energetic preference for the (E)-isomer based on pi-pi interactions.
